title: IC growth hiring flow and onboarding sprint
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for hiring mid-level to senior individual contributors (ICs) across engineering and product-adjacent roles, plus a tightly scoped 30-day onboarding sprint template. The goal: reduce time-to-impact, align interview evaluation criteria across panels, and create a repeatable onboarding sprint that helps new ICs contribute to inference-serving workstreams within 6–10 weeks.

Scope and audience:
- Roles: Senior/IC Software Engineer (serving runtime), Applied ML Engineer, Observability Engineer, Product Engineer (console).
- Owners: people-ops (recruiting + talent enablement) with hiring manager co-ownership.
- Status: draft -> iterate after 3 hires.

High-level hiring flow (one-liner steps):
1) Intake calibration (15–30m) with hiring manager + people-ops + tech lead.
2) Sourcing brief & outreach (templates below).
3) Phone screen (30m) — recruiter + cultural fit + basic scope.
4) Technical screen (60m) — take-home or live coding depending on role.
5) Onsite loop (4–5 interviews, 3–4 hours total) — rubric-driven.
6) Debrief and score (24h SLA from interviewers).
7) Offer and negotiation (people-ops lead).
8) Preboarding + first-day logistics.

Intake calibration checklist (to run in 15–30m):
- Role purpose: one-sentence impact statement (e.g., "reduce tail latency for multi-tenant hosting").
- Top 3 success metrics in 3 months, 6 months, 12 months.
- Must-have skills vs nice-to-have (specific frameworks, e.g., CUDA experience, distributed systems).
- Required interviewers and decision maker(s).
- Compensation band alignment and hiring timeline.
- Any tooling/access/security constraints for candidate assessment (e.g., no public take-homes if NDA).

Sourcing/outreach templates (short):
- Subject: "Redwood: Senior Engineer role working on inference performance"
- Body lead: "Hi <name>, I saw your work on <project>. We're shipping inference runtime optimizations that power product features and would love to chat about a senior engineer role focused on latency, batching, and observability. Quick 20-min chat?"

Phone screen guide (recruiter, 20–30m):
- 5m: intro, context, candidate brief.
- 10m: career arc, recent projects highlights.
- 5m: role fit & motivation (what excites them here?).
- 5m: logistics (comp band, start date, visa).
- Decision: pass / pass-with-conditions / no-go + suggested next steps.

Technical screen options (role dependent):
- Live: 45–60m whiteboard/problem solving (systems design / algorithm).
- Take-home: 4–8 hour task, judged on correctness, tradeoffs documentation, and clarity.
- For applied ML: short eval focusing on inference-cost/latency tradeoffs and reproducibility.

Interview loop structure (onsite — example for serving-runtime hire):
- Welcome + role context (15m) — hiring manager, product context, success metrics.
- Systems design (60m) — design for scale, SLO tradeoffs, failure modes.
- Debugging / code review (45m) — given a small repo extract, find and fix a performance bug.
- Behavioral / collaboration (30m) — cross-team examples, conflict resolution.
- Ops/observability (30m) — incident reasoning, alert tuning, tracing.
- Optional: take-home review or manager deep dive.

Debrief & scoring (required within 24h):
- Use the standardized rubric below. Each interviewer records: score (1–5), top strengths, top risks, hire/no-hire recommendation, suggested level. People-ops synthesizes for hiring manager.

Standardized rubric (flat scoring guidance):
- Problem Solving (1–5): clarity of thought, trade-offs, edge cases.
- System Design (1–5): architecture thinking, scalability, SLO-aware decisions.
- Coding Quality (1–5): correctness, readability, test thinking.
- Debugging/Tooling (1–5): practical ops instincts, telemetry use.
- Collaboration & Communication (1–5): cross-team empathy, clarity in debriefs.
- Impact & Ownership (1–5): past examples of rolling changes to prod, ownership of outcomes.
Scoring rubric guidance: 20–22 => Strong Hire; 16–19 => Hire; 12–15 => Consider with references; <12 => No hire.

Calibration session cadence (people-ops-led):
- Weekly 30m "interviewer calibration" slot for active searches: review borderline cases, revisit scoring drift, share exemplar debriefs.
- Monthly deep-dive: share 1 anonymized case study (what went well / blindspots).

Interview feedback template (for debrief form):
- Candidate name / role applied / date
- Score per rubric category (1–5)
- 3 bullet strengths
- 3 bullet risks / open questions
- Recommendation: Strong Hire | Hire | Consider | No Hire
- Suggested leveling and comp rationale

Preboarding checklist (to run immediately after offer accepted):
- Create onboarding plan doc in hiring manager's folder; share with new hire and team.
- Invite to #team slack, add to relevant Google groups, calendar invites for first 30 days.
- Provision laptop, VPN, corporate accounts, and role-specific infra access (S3, private clusters) — track through ticket ID.
- Assign onboarding buddy (peer IC) and mentor (manager or senior IC).
- Share reading list: architecture diagrams, recent incident postmortems, product roadmap snippet, codebase map.

30-day onboarding sprint (example deliverables for IC):
Week 1: ramp and access
- Complete security/training modules.
- Local dev env + run a simple end-to-end test in staging.
- 1:1s with manager, buddy, and primary cross-team partners.

Week 2: small bug/first PR
- Pick a starter issue that touches serving runtime path (low-risk perf test).
- Ship a PR, get feedback, land change in staging.

Week 3: domain deep-dive + owner area
- Deliver a short doc: "five improvement ideas for tail latency" with quick-wins + estimation.
- Present in team async channel; collect feedback.

Week 4: measurable contribution
- Own a small rollout (canary config, perf test) and report metrics.
- Update onboarding doc with lessons learned and recommended next steps.

30/60/90 goals (manager-to-candidate framing):
- 30 days: pass security/infra gates, local dev, first PR merged, team introduced.
- 60 days: own a minor feature or performance improvement end-to-end in staging.
- 90 days: take full ownership of a production metric (latency or cost) and propose a roadmap item.

Manager checklist for first 90 days (quick):
- Provide clear success metrics and 30/60/90 goals in writing.
- Weekly 1:1 + biweekly 1:many with team for socialization.
- Fast feedback loops on PRs and design docs.
- Schedule a 90-day review and a measurable objective.

Common failure modes + mitigations:
- Too many open access tickets: prioritize infra tickets preboarding, hold a "kickoff permissions" meeting.
- Interviewer score drift: run calibration within 1 week of a surprising hire/no-hire.
- New hire isolation: ensure buddy meets daily first week and group sync in week 2.

Open questions / TODOs in this doc (working list):
- Decide whether applied-ML candidates get take-home by default or only for senior roles.
- Create a short rubric cheat-sheet (1-pager) for interviewers.
- Build a post-onboarding survey to gather 30/60 day signals.

Appendix: quick links and templates
- Short PR template for starter tasks (linked in GH PR above).
- Example debrief: (anonymized) — see Confluence link.
- Slack channels: #people-ops, #eng-serving-runtime, #onboarding-buddies.

Notes on iteration: treat this doc as living. After two hires use the "calibration" slot to fold lessons into the 30-day sprint tasks and the rubric. Keep language concrete and measurable; avoid vague expectations like "ramp quickly" without metrics.

End.
